summary: Hot Spot Harmonization is a web-based platform, containing all of the data generated by MODIS and VIIRS satellites. It includes features such as world map hotspot detection, as well as multiple historic statistics regarding the fire activity in specific areas. Those summaries would be helpful for fire departments, ecologists and other people, interested in fire activity around the globe through the years. Website is deployed at http://hsh.satiscracktory.top
details:
HotSpotHarmonization (HSH)

What it does and how it works

HotSpotHarmonization is a full-stack wildfire monitoring platform. It turns NASA satellite fire-detection data into an interactive map with charts.

• Importer (HSH.Importer) loads raw NASA hotspot data into SQL Server. It also builds a spatial index for each country, made of a binary space partitioning tree and cell lookups. Imports can be stopped and resumed safely.

• Backend (HSH.API, HSH.Core, HSH.Data) is an ASP.NET Core REST API with these endpoints:

– fire locations for a country over a time period of up to 31 days

– a count of actual fire events, made by grouping neighbouring detections with a grid-based flood-fill

– fires inside a selected rectangle on the map, found quickly through the spatial index

• Frontend (HSH.Client) is a React app. It shows fires on an interactive Leaflet map, lets users filter by country and date, and uses Chart.js charts to show statistics and trends.

Benefits and intended impact

The platform turns millions of raw satellite records into clear, visual information. Grouping neighbouring detections gives realistic fire counts, and spatial indexing keeps map queries fast. It aims to help researchers, emergency services, environmental groups and the public understand wildfire activity and support planning and response.

Tools and technologies

• Backend: C# 14, .NET 10, ASP.NET Core Web API, Entity Framework Core, ASP.NET Identity

• Database: Microsoft SQL Server

• Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet / React-Leaflet (map), Chart.js / react-chartjs-2 (charts), React Router, world-countries (country data)

• Data source: NASA satellite fire data

• Development tools: Visual Studio, VS Code, ESLint, Git/GitHub. No special hardware is needed.

What makes it creative

The project uses classic algorithms on a real environmental problem: a k-d/BSP tree for spatial search and graph flood-fill to group detections into fires. The expensive work happens once at import time, so the API and the interactive map stay responsive.

Factors the team considered

• Performance: spatial indexes and database indexes to handle very large data

• Accuracy: counting fire events rather than raw detections

• Protecting the server: a limit on the time range per request

• Reliability: imports that can be restarted after an interruption

• Maintainability: separate Data, Core, API, Importer and Client layers

• Usability: a clear, visual frontend for non-technical users
